record.paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
record.original_question: For tree-level string cosmologies containing Ramond-Ramond fields, what are the asymptotic properties of the resulting universes, are the known solutions stable and unique, and do there exist solutions that appear only subdominantly in the asymptotic regime in a way that constrains the allowed singular asymptotic states?

evidence.quote:
2.2 Asymptotics of speciﬁc tree-level string actions II
The problem here is to study the asymptotic properties of universes with RR ﬁelds. This asymptotic analysis will tell us about the stability of the known solutions, whether they are unique. It is possible that there are solutions which exist only subdominantly asymptotically and these are expected to be identiﬁed by our analysis.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider tree-level low-energy effective string actions in $D$ spacetime dimensions that, in addition to the metric $g_{\mu\nu}$ and dilaton $\phi$, contain one or more Ramond–Ramond (RR) $p$-form field strengths $F_{(p)} = dA_{(p-1)}$. A representative bosonic sector is

$$ S = \frac{1}{2\kappa^2}\int d^Dx\,\sqrt{-g}\,\left[ e^{-2\phi}\left(R + 4(\nabla\phi)^2\right) - \sum_p \frac{1}{2\,p!}\,F_{(p)}^2 \right], $$

with the RR field strengths entering without a dilaton prefactor (in the string frame). Restrict to spatially homogeneous and isotropic cosmological ansätze, e.g.
$$ ds^2 = -dt^2 + a(t)^2\, d\Sigma_k^2, \qquad \phi = \phi(t), \qquad F_{(p)} = F_{(p)}(t), $$
where $d\Sigma_k^2$ is a maximally symmetric spatial metric of curvature $k\in\{-1,0,+1\}$, and let the equations of motion be the resulting autonomous system of ODEs for $(a,\phi,F_{(p)})$.

Establish a complete asymptotic analysis of this dynamical system in the regimes $t\to t_*$ corresponding to cosmological singularities (initial or final). Specifically:

(a) Classify all asymptotic (singular) behaviours of the solutions: determine the possible scaling exponents and leading-order forms of $a(t)$, $\phi(t)$, and $F_{(p)}(t)$ near a singularity, and identify the dominant and subdominant branches.

(b) Decide whether each known closed-form solution (e.g. dilaton–RR rolling-radii solutions, power-law attractors) is dynamically stable as an asymptotic regime, and whether it is unique within its branch up to the obvious symmetries (time translation, time reversal, rescaling).

(c) Identify any solutions that exist only as subdominant asymptotic regimes — i.e. solutions whose contribution is sub-leading compared with a dominant attractor — and determine in what way their existence constrains the set of admissible singular asymptotic states of universes containing RR fields.
artifact.status_search_result: A comprehensive asymptotic classification of tree-level string cosmologies including Ramond–Ramond fields, addressing stability, uniqueness, and subdominant branches, does not appear in the literature. Related but partial results exist: tree-level NS–NS string cosmology has been analyzed (Copeland–Lahiri–Wands, 1996), and asymptotic scalar field cosmology in string theory (Rudelius 2022, Calderón-Infante et al.) treats late-time attractors via the Distance/Swampland conjectures, but not a full singular-asymptotic classification with explicit RR-form sources. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Tree-level string cosmology (Copeland, Lahiri, Wands)
status_evidence.snippet: Classical evolution of cosmological models from low-energy tree-level limits of string theory; generic solutions begin or end with singularities and dilaton diverges.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier work treats tree-level NS–NS cases but does not give a complete asymptotic classification including RR fields.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotic Scalar Field Cosmology in String Theory (Rudelius)
status_evidence.snippet: Late-time cosmology in infinite-distance limits of scalar field space featuring exponential potentials and towers of states.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses asymptotic scalar cosmology but does not classify singular asymptotics of RR-coupled tree-level systems.

status_evidence.title: The Singularity Problem in Brane Cosmology
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of singularity resolution and asymptotic states in higher-dimensional/string-inspired cosmologies.
status_evidence.claim: Singularity classification in such systems remains an active and unresolved problem.
